meta.title: Many Worlds Cloud: cloud infrastructure deep visibility
meta.description: Cloud reads what a security scan has found in your AWS, Azure and Google Cloud accounts and turns it into a report and a list of things to act on: risks, incidents and tasks.

hero.title: Know what is exposed in your cloud, and what to do about it.
hero.text: Cloud reads what a security scan has found in your cloud accounts and turns it into a report and a list of things to act on.

tally.label: views of one report: leadership, cloud owners, the people doing the work
platforms in one picture: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes and Microsoft 365
lists to act on: risks, incidents and tasks

table_note: Illustration of the report. The product is in development and every figure is invented.

sections.label: It only reads
sections.title: Nothing is installed in your cloud, and nothing in it is changed.
sections.text: A scanner looks at how your cloud accounts are set up, using a role that can read and nothing more. Cloud takes what the scanner found and makes it readable. It never creates, changes or deletes a resource, and it fixes nothing on its own.
points: The scanner is Prowler, the open-source cloud security scanner, and stays a separate system
AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes and Microsoft 365 in the same report
Hundreds of checks: identity, storage, networks, encryption, logging

sections.label: Can these results be trusted?
sections.title: The report starts by saying how completely each account could be scanned.
sections.text: An account that looks clean because the scanner was refused access must never read as an account with nothing wrong. So every report opens with what was scanned, when, and which checks could not run, and says whether the figures below are complete or lower bounds.

cells: Lower bound: no permission to read the key vaults
Not scanned: the credentials have expired

points: Accounts scanned, and when each was last scanned
Checks that could not run, and the permission each one was missing
If a scan fails, the report still builds and says what is missing

sections.label: Findings, ranked by severity
sections.title: Each finding comes with why it matters, what to do and the evidence.
sections.text: A finding is something in your cloud that needs a decision. The worst come first, and each one names the resources behind it.

cells: Storage readable by anyone on the internet
The root account has no second sign-in factor
A database can be reached from the internet
Audit logging is off in two regions
Turn on logging in every region

points: Open storage, administrators without multi-factor authentication, old access keys, databases facing the internet
Trends against the scan before, so you can see whether risk is going up or down
PDF, Excel and PowerPoint from every page

sections.label: One report, three readers
sections.title: Leadership and cloud owners ask different questions. Each gets its own view.
sections.text: The executive summary answers in a page. The cloud owner view goes down to the single resource. The full report carries the evidence for whoever does the work.

columns.title: Questions for leadership
items: Is risk going up or down?
Do we know what is running in our cloud?
Is anything open to the internet that should not be?
Are logs kept, so an incident can be investigated?
Where do we stand against the frameworks we answer to?

columns.title: Questions for cloud owners
items: What changed since the scan before?
Which failures are new, and which were fixed?
Which keys and roles are unused or too powerful?
Which network rules are open to everyone?
What is the fix for each finding?

sections.label: Compliance
sections.title: The same findings, read against the frameworks you answer to.
sections.text: One scan answers many auditors. Cloud shows which requirements of each framework are met, which are failing and which could not be assessed, with the findings behind every one.
points: Frameworks such as CIS, ISO 27001, NIS2, GDPR, SOC 2, PCI DSS and ENS
A failing requirement opens the findings that caused it
Not assessed is never shown as met

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.title: The report ends in three lists somebody can act on.
sections.text: Risks go to a register, incidents to a SOC, tasks to a queue. Every rating carries the rule that produced it, because these are first readings from one scan and the page says so.

boxes.d: A standing weakness, rated likelihood times consequence, each from 1 to 5, and given to an owner.
Something that is exposed right now and needs responding to.
One piece of work with a queue, a due date and a way to tell when it is finished.

points: Send the three lists to a SpaceRisk register with one button. Nothing is sent until it is pressed
Sending again updates what was sent before and never makes a second copy
Exports for a SIEM (OCSF) and for Jira, ServiceNow or a mailbox, plus Excel and PowerPoint

sections.label: Every account at once
sections.title: Rank your cloud accounts by what needs deciding.
sections.text: With more than one account, subscription or project you get them side by side: which needs attention first, what is true at several of them against what is true at one, and which could not be scanned completely.
points: Each row opens that account's own report
Findings shared by several accounts are shown together
Unscanned is never shown as clean

contact.title: See Cloud read your own accounts.
contact.text: Tell us about your cloud and we will show you the report on simulated data first, then on yours.
